foundation.def: The solid base of grammar, vocabulary, and structural understanding upon which further language fluency is built.
foundation.quote: Louie (02:22): "Your English has a very strong foundation and structure. You clearly have a logical process in mind."

counterpart.def: A colleague or professional holding a corresponding position or function in another team, office, or organization.
counterpart.quote: Louie (02:37): "When explaining how you interact with different counterparts and stakeholders, you are actually quite quick at answering."

stakeholder.def: Any individual, department, client, or group that has an active interest or stake in the outcome of a business process.
stakeholder.quote: Louie (02:37): "...dealing with different counterparts, different stakeholders across the company."

imitate.def: To naturally copy the cadence, rhythm, or phrasing of native speech to develop ease and muscle memory.
imitate.quote: Louie (03:31): "You will start to imitate natural cadences, and fluency becomes second nature."

second-nature.def: A behavior or habit that has become so instinctive and automatic through practice that it requires no conscious effort.
second-nature.quote: Louie (03:31): "...fluency becomes second nature through gentle, natural conversation."
second-nature.it: una seconda natura / qualcosa di spontaneo

troubleshoot.def: To trace, diagnose, and resolve technical problems or defects in machinery, software, or operating systems.
troubleshoot.quote: Simone (04:37): "I work in technical support, so my job is to troubleshoot and resolve problems for our customers."

rebuttal.def: In rhetoric or discourse, a swift, structured response or reply addressing a question or argument.
rebuttal.quote: Louie (05:14): "Your rebuttal—your answering—is great. You're very quick and you give precise answers."

trade-off.def: A situational decision where one acceptable benefit is given up in return for gaining a different desirable quality.
trade-off.quote: Simone (06:14): "It's a sort of balance between two or more things." / Louie: "You balance one benefit against another."

bottleneck.def: A stage in an operation or production pipeline where capacity is constrained, causing overall delays.
bottleneck.quote: Louie (08:12): "A bottleneck is when one stage of a process or operation cannot keep up with the rest."

take-the-pressure-off.def: To relieve someone of tension, anxiety, or heavy expectations so they can feel comfortable and relaxed.
take-the-pressure-off.quote: Louie (11:28): "It takes the pressure off of taking notes in the lesson and missing something."
take-the-pressure-off.it: togliere la pressione / alleggerire lo stress

recap.def: To briefly review, summarize, or restate the main points of a discussion or study session.
recap.quote: Louie (12:43): "Notes are very easy to recap and go over at the end of the lesson or whenever you're available."

in-the-loop.def: Kept fully informed, updated, and involved in ongoing communications or project decisions.
in-the-loop.quote: Simone (13:54): "In the mail context, if someone is added to an email thread, they are in the loop."
in-the-loop.it: al corrente / nel giro delle comunicazioni

out-of-the-loop.def: Excluded from important information, unaware of developments, or omitted from updates.
out-of-the-loop.quote: Simone (13:54) & Louie (14:14): "And out of the loop is just not getting the information or communication."

free-form.def: Not conforming to a rigid structure or predetermined script; spontaneous, organic, and open.
free-form.quote: Louie (14:24): "I also believe in free-form conversation because we learn way more information."

first-course.def: The opening substantial dish of a formal meal, such as pasta, soup, or risotto (equivalent to Italian 'il primo').
first-course.quote: Simone (17:40): "This is a typical first course in Italy that we often prepare with mushrooms—risotto."

vine.def: A climbing woody-stemmed plant that supports bunches of grapes for eating or winemaking.
vine.quote: Louie (18:38): "We say in England, grapes grow on vines (V-I-N-E-S)."

glow.def: To emit a steady, soft, radiant light without producing sparks or fire.
glow.quote: Louie (19:35): "It's a small little bug, and it glows in the dark."

firefly.def: A soft-bodied nocturnal beetle capable of producing bioluminescent flashes from its abdomen.
firefly.quote: Louie (19:51): "It's a firefly—a bioluminescent flying beetle."

nectar.def: A sugar-rich fluid secreted by flowering plants to encourage pollination by insects and birds.
nectar.quote: Louie (20:00): "This bird flies very fast and it drinks nectar from blossoms."

hummingbird.def: A tiny, iridescent American bird capable of hovering mid-air by beating its wings up to 80 times per second.
hummingbird.quote: Louie (20:20): "It's a hummingbird (colibri in Italian)! It moves so rapidly it appears to hover in place."

whereabouts.def: In or near what approximate place or area.
whereabouts.quote: Louie (20:38): "Whereabouts in Italy are you located?"
whereabouts.it: in che zona / dove di preciso

restoration.def: The meticulous trade or art of repairing and returning ancient architecture to its authentic historic condition.
restoration.quote: Louie (20:49): "Before moving to Vietnam, I worked in historical restoration, rebuilding old buildings 600–700 years old."

spare-time.def: Free time outside of career responsibilities, family care, and household chores.
spare-time.quote: Louie (22:06): "What do you like to do in your spare time?"

relatives.def: Members of one's extended family (cousins, uncles, aunts, grandparents). Distinct from 'parents' (mother and father).
relatives.quote: Louie (23:51): "In English we say relatives for extended family, whereas 'parents' refers strictly to mother and father."

turn-red.def: To blush intensely on one's face as a reaction to sudden shock, surprise, or emotional intensity.
turn-red.quote: Simone (24:14): "When the doctor said it to me and my wife, I turned totally red from shock!"

special-bond.def: A rare, profound mutual understanding and protective emotional closeness between two people.
special-bond.quote: Louie (24:46): "Twins share a special bond that lasts a lifetime. It is truly magical."

siblings.def: Brothers or sisters; individuals who share the same parents.
siblings.quote: Louie (25:27): "Do you have siblings yourself? Brothers and sisters?"
siblings.it: fratelli e sorelle (fratelli in senso neutro)

competitive.def: Involving passionate rivalry and strategic skill aimed at testing oneself against other players.
competitive.quote: Simone (26:55): "It is very competitive because you enter in a team of three people to win against another team."

cinematic.def: Possessing the sweeping visual majesty, camera direction, and narrative weight of high-budget film.
cinematic.quote: Louie (27:47): "I like the cinematic feel of God of War—it feels like being inside a magnificent movie."

mechanics.def: The underlying systems, rule engines, and structural dynamics that dictate how a tabletop or digital game functions.
mechanics.quote: Louie (31:02): "Describing the mechanics of the games, what we like about how they work."

abroad.def: In or traveling to foreign countries across national borders.
abroad.quote: Simone (32:02): "And one couple is often abroad, so it's difficult to meet up all together."

lifelong.def: Enduring, continuing, or remaining constant across an entire human lifespan.
lifelong.quote: Simone (33:04): "I know my best friend from my birth—our families were friends, so we have had a lifelong friendship."

civilization.def: An advanced society with complex cultural, urban, economic, and scientific achievements.
civilization.quote: Simone (33:49): "Then you use these cards to build your civilization across the ages."

victory-points.def: The definitive numerical score units accumulated in modern Euro and strategy tabletop games to decide the winner.
victory-points.quote: Simone (33:49): "It's a building game where you have to collect victory points through smart drafting."

card-drafting.def: A board game mechanism where players pick one card from a hand and pass the remaining hand to their neighbor.
card-drafting.quote: Simone (33:49): "To collect points, you have to draft some cards—select one and pass the deck to the next player."
card-drafting.it: card drafting / selezione e passaggio carte

combo.def: A clever combination of card synergies, abilities, or moves that amplify each other's effects.
combo.quote: Simone (34:51): "You can use these cards to build the combo to score the highest points."

era.def: A distinct epoch or stage of history marked by notable characteristics or developmental progress.
era.quote: Simone (34:51): "There are three distinct eras or ages in the game."

evolution.def: The continuous, gradual process of change, adaptation, and refinement in rules, traditions, or systems.
evolution.quote: Louie (39:22): "With custom rules, the game is always changing and evolving into new variations."

to-no-avail.def: Without success, effect, or positive result despite earnest efforts.
to-no-avail.quote: Louie (39:22): "I always promise myself I'll keep quiet, but to no avail—I always talk too much!"

subscription.def: A recurring payment agreement granting continuous access to an entertainment service or digital library.
subscription.quote: Simone (42:18): "We don't have the HBO subscription yet, but she really wants to get it."

adaptation.def: A film, television, or theatrical recreation crafted from an original literary text or novel.
adaptation.quote: Louie (43:51): "The Prisoner of Azkaban movie is such a stylish adaptation—very entertaining."

trilogy.def: A coordinated collection of three literary or cinematic creations forming a continuous narrative saga.
trilogy.quote: Simone (44:25): "I read the entire trilogy of The Lord of the Rings before the films finished coming out."

honeymoon.def: A celebratory holiday taken by a newly wedded couple immediately following their marriage ceremony.
honeymoon.quote: Simone (45:10): "When my wife and I got married, we spent our honeymoon road-tripping through New Zealand!"
honeymoon.it: luna di miele / viaggio di nozze

itinerary.def: A comprehensive planned schedule of destinations, dates, and routes arranged for an expedition.
itinerary.quote: Louie (45:25): "What was your itinerary, your travel route across the North Island?"

scenery.def: The majestic natural physical panorama of mountains, meadows, and vistas in a countryside region.
scenery.quote: Simone (46:02): "The rolling green scenery of New Zealand was breathtaking."

fantasy.def: A narrative genre characterized by magical realms, imaginary mythologies, and heroic quests.
fantasy.quote: Simone (46:58): "It's strange to see a place you know is a fantasy place, yet you are physically there."

dense.def: Packed tightly with extensive detail, historical exposition, and poetic lore; challenging to read quickly.
dense.quote: Louie (47:47): "Reading Lord of the Rings can be so dense with lore and poetry—it takes serious dedication."

tongue-tied.def: Unable to speak easily, fluently, or freely because of sudden shyness, nervousness, or searching for vocabulary.
tongue-tied.quote: Simone (49:25): "Sometimes when I speak English, I feel tongue-tied because I search for a specific word and can't find it."
tongue-tied.it: con la lingua legata / bloccato nel parlare

freeze-up.def: To suddenly become unable to speak or continue a conversation because of performance anxiety or self-doubt.
freeze-up.quote: Simone (49:25): "And then I freeze up in the conversation when I can't locate the exact term."

food-for-thought.def: Stimulating insights, ideas, or experiences worthy of quiet reflection and future application.
food-for-thought.quote: Louie (50:17): "Chatting about board games and real experiences gives us plenty of food for thought."
food-for-thought.it: spunto di riflessione / cibo per la mente

extended-family.def: A family structure branching beyond parents and children to encompass aunts, uncles, cousins, and in-laws.
extended-family.quote: Louie (23:51): "...extended family like cousins and grandparents."
